newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Futures Exchange revises stock futures margins.
newsitem.headline: HK Futures Exchange revises stock futures margins.

text.p: The Hong Kong Futures Exchange said on Wednesday it will revise the margin rates for its three stock futures contracts from February 14 based on the recent performance of the underlying stocks.
The exchange said it will lift the initial and maintenance margin for HSBC Holdings Plc and Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd contracts.
The initial and maintenance margin on Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd will be revised downwards, it said in a statement.
The initial margin for HSBC will be raised to HK$25,000 from HK$17,000 and the maintenance margin to HK$20,000 from HK$13,500, the exchange said.
The initial margin on Cheung Kong contracts will be increased to HK$30,000 from HK$20,000 and the maintenance margin to HK$24,000 from HK$16,000.
For Hongkong Telecom contracts, the initial margin will be lowered to HK$10,000 from HK$13,000 and the maintenance margin to HK$8,000 from HK$10,000.
A spokesman said the exchange would monitor volatility of the underlying stocks for future contracts and revise margins from time to time to keep trading risk under control.

He also said stock futures contracts, which are only available on the three blue-chip companies, will start electronic automated trading from February with the introduction of a new market-making system to boost activity.
Timber Hill Hong Kong Ltd has signed up as a market maker for the product, he said.
